questions.title: Whose Branch?
questions.story_md:
Tall buildings have more floors to hide in.

Return **account id**, **owner** and the **branch name** for accounts whose branch has **at least {floors}** floors.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE branches (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, city TEXT, opened TEXT, floors INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT a.id, a.owner, b.name FROM accounts a JOIN branches b ON b.id = a.branch_id WHERE b.floors >= {floors};

hints.text: JOIN branches ON branches.id = accounts.branch_id
Filter on the branch floors.

questions.title: Who Opened It?
questions.story_md:
The vault log only stores employee ids.

Return the **first_name**, **last_name** and **at** date of every **{action}** in zone **{zone}**.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE vault_logs (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, action TEXT, zone TEXT, at TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, l.at FROM vault_logs l JOIN employees e ON e.id = l.employee_id WHERE l.action = {action|sql} AND l.zone = {zone|sql};

hints.text: Join the log to employees on employee_id.

questions.title: Big Movers
questions.story_md:
Large transfers deserve a closer look.

Return **owner**, **amount** and **at** for transactions over **{min_amount}**.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT a.owner, t.amount, t.at FROM transactions t JOIN accounts a ON a.id = t.account_id WHERE t.amount > {min_amount};

hints.text: Join transactions to accounts on account_id.

questions.title: Branch Reserves
questions.story_md:
Which building holds the most?

Return **branch name** and **total balance** of its accounts — one row per branch (by id) that has at least one account.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE branches (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, city TEXT, opened TEXT, floors INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT b.name, SUM(a.balance) FROM branches b JOIN accounts a ON a.branch_id = b.id GROUP BY b.id;

hints.text: Join, then GROUP BY the branch.
Group by branch id: names can repeat.

questions.title: Debtors
questions.story_md:
People with **{status}** loans are desperate.

Return **owner**, **loan amount** and **rate** for loans with that status.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE loans (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, rate REAL, status TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT a.owner, l.amount, l.rate FROM loans l JOIN accounts a ON a.id = l.account_id WHERE l.status = {status|sql};

hints.text: loans.account_id points at accounts.id.

questions.title: Busy Departments
questions.story_md:
Which departments touch the vault most?

Return **dept** and the **number of vault log entries** made by its employees.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE vault_logs (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, action TEXT, zone TEXT, at TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT e.dept, COUNT(*) FROM vault_logs l JOIN employees e ON e.id = l.employee_id GROUP BY e.dept;

hints.text: Join first, then group by the department.

questions.title: Same Building
questions.story_md:
Who works in the same branch as employee **{emp}**?

Return **id** and **first_name** of every *other* employee with the same branch_id.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT o.id, o.first_name FROM employees e JOIN employees o ON o.branch_id = e.branch_id AND o.id <> e.id WHERE e.id = {emp};

hints.text: Join employees to itself with two aliases.

questions.title: Sleeping Accounts
questions.story_md:
Dormant accounts are never checked.

Return **id** and **owner** of accounts with **no transactions at all**.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT a.id, a.owner FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN transactions t ON t.account_id = a.id WHERE t.id IS NULL;

hints.text: LEFT JOIN keeps accounts without matches.
Unmatched rows have NULL on the right side.

questions.title: Never Been Inside
questions.story_md:
Staff who never entered the vault won't recognise you.

Return **id**, **first_name** and **dept** of employees with **no vault log entries**.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE vault_logs (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, action TEXT, zone TEXT, at TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT e.id, e.first_name, e.dept FROM employees e LEFT JOIN vault_logs l ON l.employee_id = e.id WHERE l.id IS NULL;

hints.text: LEFT JOIN, then WHERE right_side.id IS NULL.

questions.title: Activity Report
questions.story_md:
Every account, even the quiet ones.

Return **account id** and its **number of transactions** — accounts with none must show **0**.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT a.id, COUNT(t.id) FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN transactions t ON t.account_id = a.id GROUP BY a.id;

hints.text: COUNT(t.id) counts only matched rows; COUNT(*) would count 1 for empty accounts.

questions.title: Total Debt
questions.story_md:
Owners of **{type}** accounts: how much do they owe?

Return **account id** and **total loan amount** — show **0** for accounts without loans.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE loans (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, rate REAL, status TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT a.id, COALESCE(SUM(l.amount), 0) FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN loans l ON l.account_id = a.id WHERE a.type = {type|sql} GROUP BY a.id;

hints.text: COALESCE(x, 0) turns NULL into 0.

questions.title: Cash Only
questions.story_md:
Transactions with no merchant are cash.

Return **id** and **amount** of transactions on account **{account}** whose merchant is **missing (NULL)**.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, amount FROM transactions WHERE account_id = {account} AND merchant IS NULL;

hints.text: = NULL never matches; use IS NULL.

questions.title: Quiet Days
questions.story_md:
Which employees had no shift on **{day}**?

Return **id** and **first_name** of employees without a shift that day.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE shifts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, day TEXT, shift TEXT, hours INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT e.id, e.first_name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN shifts s ON s.employee_id = e.id AND s.day = {day|sql} WHERE s.id IS NULL;

hints.text: Put the day filter in the ON clause, not WHERE.
Otherwise the LEFT JOIN behaves like an INNER JOIN.

questions.title: Follow the City
questions.story_md:
Trace money back to buildings.

Return **transaction id**, **amount** and **branch city** for **{kind}** transactions over **{min_amount}**.
questions.reference_sql: SELECT t.id, t.amount, b.city FROM transactions t JOIN accounts a ON a.id = t.account_id JOIN branches b ON b.id = a.branch_id WHERE t.kind = {kind|sql} AND t.amount > {min_amount};

hints.text: transactions → accounts → branches: two JOINs.

questions.title: City Volume
questions.story_md:
Which city moves the most money?

Return **city** and the **total transaction amount** across all its branches' accounts.
questions.reference_sql: SELECT b.city, SUM(t.amount) FROM transactions t JOIN accounts a ON a.id = t.account_id JOIN branches b ON b.id = a.branch_id GROUP BY b.city;

hints.text: Join three tables, group by city.

questions.title: Risky Branch
questions.story_md:
High-rate loans point to a sloppy branch.

Return **branch name**, **owner** and **rate** for loans with rate above **{rate}**.
questions.reference_sql: SELECT b.name, a.owner, l.rate FROM loans l JOIN accounts a ON a.id = l.account_id JOIN branches b ON b.id = a.branch_id WHERE l.rate > {rate};

hints.text: loans → accounts → branches.

questions.title: Shift Overlap
questions.story_md:
Who was on a **{shift}** shift *and* touched the vault that same day?

Return **distinct employee id** and **first_name** for employees with a vault log entry on a day they worked a **{shift}** shift.
questions.reference_sql: SELECT DISTINCT e.id, e.first_name FROM employees e JOIN shifts s ON s.employee_id = e.id JOIN vault_logs l ON l.employee_id = e.id AND l.at = s.day WHERE s.shift = {shift|sql};

hints.text: Join logs on both employee_id and date.

questions.title: Big Spenders
questions.story_md:
Owners who once moved more than **{amount}** in one go.

Return **id** and **owner** of accounts that have **any** transaction over that amount.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, owner FROM accounts WHERE id IN (SELECT account_id FROM transactions WHERE amount > {amount});

hints.text: WHERE id IN (SELECT account_id FROM …)

questions.title: Never Withdrew
questions.story_md:
Savers never take money out.

Return **id** and **owner** of accounts that **never** made a withdrawal.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, amount INTEGER, at TEXT, merchant TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, owner FROM accounts WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT account_id FROM transactions WHERE kind = 'withdrawal');

hints.text: NOT IN (subquery) — watch out if the subquery could return NULL.

questions.title: Vault Visitors
questions.story_md:
Who visited zone **{zone}**?

Return **id** and **first_name** of employees for whom **a vault log entry exists** in that zone.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE vault_logs (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, action TEXT, zone TEXT, at TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT e.id, e.first_name FROM employees e WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM vault_logs l WHERE l.employee_id = e.id AND l.zone = {zone|sql});

hints.text: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM … WHERE matches outer row)

questions.title: Clean Record
questions.story_md:
Employees with **no {action}** entries are trusted.

Return **id** and **last_name** of employees with no vault log entry of that action.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE vault_logs (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, action TEXT, zone TEXT, at TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT e.id, e.last_name FROM employees e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM vault_logs l WHERE l.employee_id = e.id AND l.action = {action|sql});

hints.text: NOT EXISTS keeps rows with no match.

questions.title: Branch Watch
questions.story_md:
Branches opened before **{year}** still use old locks.

Return **id** and **balance** of accounts that belong to any branch opened before **{year}-01-01**.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE branches (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, city TEXT, opened TEXT, floors INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, balance FROM accounts WHERE branch_id IN (SELECT id FROM branches WHERE opened < {year} || '-01-01');

hints.text: Subquery returns the branch ids.
Compare dates as text: opened < '2005-01-01'.

questions.title: Frozen Debts
questions.story_md:
Loans on frozen accounts can't be collected.

Return **loan id** and **amount** of loans whose account has status **frozen**.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE loans (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, rate REAL, status TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT id, amount FROM loans WHERE account_id IN (SELECT id FROM accounts WHERE status = 'frozen');

hints.text: Find frozen account ids in a subquery.

questions.title: Above Average
questions.story_md:
Above-average earners have more access.

Return **first_name** and **salary** of employees paid **more than the company average**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT first_name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);

hints.text: Compare with (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees).

questions.title: Crown Jewel
questions.story_md:
Find the single most valuable thing in zone **{zone}**.

Return **tag**, **item** and **value** of the item(s) in that zone whose value equals the zone's maximum.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE vault_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item TEXT, value INTEGER, zone TEXT, weight_kg REAL, tag TEXT);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT tag, item, value FROM vault_items WHERE zone = {zone|sql} AND value = (SELECT MAX(value) FROM vault_items WHERE zone = {zone|sql});

hints.text: A subquery can return one value to compare against.

questions.title: Slice of the Pie
questions.story_md:
How much of all the money sits in **{type}** accounts?

Return one number: their total balance as a **percentage of all balances, rounded to 2 decimals**.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, type TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT, status TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(balance) / (SELECT SUM(balance) FROM accounts), 2) FROM accounts WHERE type = {type|sql};

hints.text: Divide by (SELECT SUM(balance) FROM accounts).
Use 100.0 to avoid integer division.

questions.title: Wanted List
questions.story_md:
Make one list of everyone flagged.

Return the **distinct employee ids** who either **{action}ed** in zone **{zone}** OR worked a **night** shift (use UNION).
questions.reference_sql: SELECT employee_id FROM vault_logs WHERE action = {action|sql} AND zone = {zone|sql} UNION SELECT employee_id FROM shifts WHERE shift = 'night';

hints.text: UNION combines and removes duplicates.

questions.title: Both Sides
questions.story_md:
Who works days *and* nights?

Return the **employee ids** that appear in both **{a}** shifts and **{b}** shifts.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE shifts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, day TEXT, shift TEXT, hours INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT employee_id FROM shifts WHERE shift = {a|sql} INTERSECT SELECT employee_id FROM shifts WHERE shift = {b|sql};

hints.text: INTERSECT keeps rows in both results.

questions.title: Never on Nights
questions.story_md:
Day-only workers don't know the night routine.

Return **employee ids** who worked a **{shift}** shift but **never** a **night** shift.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, hired TEXT, branch_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE shifts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER, day TEXT, shift TEXT, hours INTEGER);
questions.reference_sql: SELECT employee_id FROM shifts WHERE shift = {shift|sql} EXCEPT SELECT employee_id FROM shifts WHERE shift = 'night';

hints.text: EXCEPT removes rows found in the second query.

questions.title: Money Trail
questions.story_md:
One timeline of money movements for account **{account}**.

Return **date** and **amount** from its transactions, plus one row per loan of that account using date `2025-06-30` and the **loan amount**. Keep duplicates (UNION ALL).
questions.reference_sql: SELECT at, amount FROM transactions WHERE account_id = {account} UNION ALL SELECT '2025-06-30', amount FROM loans WHERE account_id = {account};

hints.text: UNION ALL keeps every row, including duplicates.
